samples.summary: Repair tests assert only the in-place mutation of the request object, never that the repaired body is what is persisted/echoed
samples.evidence: All three new repair tests (line 1242 text-element data, 1298 table cell body) force `documentService.getDocumentOrThrow.mockRejectedValue(new NotFoundException('sentinel'))`, so the controller aborts before any write, and the assertions read back the same object literal the test passed in (`body.slides[0].elements[0].data.blocks`). The write path is mocked away, so nothing proves the repaired shape reaches `writeSlidesRoot`/the response — the very claim the earlier sibling test's comment makes ('the repaired body is what reaches the writer (and what the endpoint echoes back)', line 1125-1126). The tests would pass identically if the controller discarded the validated object and re-parsed the raw payload for persistence.
searchedFor: grep 'toHaveBeenCalledWith' in spec (only earlier docs-arm tests)

samples.summary: New non-object table-cell guard (`!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)`) has no test
samples.evidence: The delta replaces the old `(cells[c] as {body?:unknown})?.body` read with an explicit cell-shape guard that silently `continue`s for null/primitive/array cells. No test in docs-content.controller.spec.ts passes a non-object cell (grep for 'cells: [' shows only `{ body: {} }`, `{ style: {} }` fixtures at lines 1207 and 1318). Whether a bogus cell is skipped rather than crashing/rejecting is therefore unverified.

samples.summary: Only an array is tested for the new non-object `data` rejection on text elements; primitive `data` (string/number/boolean) untested
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` now throws for any non-object `data` on a `text` element (controller.ts:631). Previously such a payload was silently skipped by `if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;`, so this is a newly reachable 400 for e.g. `data: 'x'` or `data: 5`. The only test of the new throw is `withTextElement([])` (spec:1286). No test covers the primitive case, which is the branch that changed behaviour for the widest set of payloads.

samples.summary: Test comment claims layout placeholders reach the same absent-`data` repair, but no test covers a placeholder/staticElement with absent data
samples.evidence: The comment at spec:1247-1248 asserts 'Group children and layout placeholders reach the same walk', yet the test body only exercises a slide-level text element and a group child. Grep for 'placeholders' in the spec (lines 919, 946, 1103) shows placeholders are only used with a fully-formed `data.blocks`; none omits `data`. The nested/identity-free path for layouts is thus documented-but-untested for this repair.

samples.summary: Explicit `data: null` on a text element is not covered; only the absent (`undefined`) case is
samples.evidence: controller.ts:627 repairs both `undefined` and `null`, but the test at spec:1259 supplies `{ id: 'e1', type: 'text', frame: {} }` (absent only). JSON round-trips of legacy decks are the stated motivation and `null` is how JSON spells absence (see spec:968-971), so the null case deserves a fixture.
